name: Deafheaven
label: Deathwish
lede: George Clarke and Kerry McCoy met in a Modesto rainstorm, recorded a $500 demo, and three years later had a pink album cover that got black metal argued about in places that never cover it.

eras.title: A Slayer shirt in the rain
eras.text: Two friends from Modesto moved to San Francisco and recorded four songs for $500. About eight shows later, a Boston hardcore label signed them.

years.h: [[George Clarke|7164a191-46a2-41c6-a696-ccb4263e95a0]] and [[Kerry McCoy|23a98713-9978-43b7-989e-625f563f7d20]] start Deafheaven when their grindcore band runs dry
years.p: Rise of Caligula had run out of direction, so the two friends moved to San Francisco and started over. Clarke has said the name is a nod to Slowdive.
years.xp:
McCoy told Red Bull Music Academy how they met in ninth grade in Modesto: "He was sitting in the open rain by himself in a Slayer t-shirt." McCoy walked over to ask about the shirt.

Wikipedia reports that Clarke has said the name is an homage to Slowdive, while acknowledging the phrase also appears in a Shakespeare sonnet.

years.h: Clarke and McCoy borrow the gear to record a $500 demo
years.p: They cut four songs at Atomic Garden Studios with engineer [[Jack Shirley|54a46dd4-403c-4f54-a12e-351dc9ff9e92]]. Neither owned an electric guitar or an amp.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the untitled demo blended black metal and post-rock, and came out digitally and on limited cassette. The band posted it on a personal Facebook profile literally named Deaf Heaven, before bands had pages, and interest came fast.

The Red Bull Music Academy interview says the band had played only eight shows before the label called.

years.h: Deafheaven becomes a five-piece and plays its first shows
years.p: Bassist Derek Prine, guitarist Nick Bassett of Whirr and drummer Trevor Deschryver join Clarke and McCoy. The lineup was partly found on Craigslist.

years.h: Deathwish phones while McCoy is working at a Ben & Jerry's
years.p: [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]]'s Deathwish Inc. first wanted only to release the demo, then agreed to put out new material too. A 7-inch with "Libertine Dissolves" and "Daedalus" went to webstore customers.
years.xp:
McCoy told Red Bull Music Academy he was at the Ben & Jerry's on Haight and Ashbury when Clarke called with the news. The band had played about eight shows.

Bannon founded Deathwish and sings in [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]].

eras.title: Roads to Judah, then three and a half months of road
eras.text: The first album lands on year-end lists. The road takes the original rhythm section.

years.h: A converted loading dock in Bell Gardens, on camera
years.p: The January 15 show at The Blacktop is filmed and later released in full as Live at The Blacktop in July 2011.

years.h: Roads to Judah, named for a San Francisco light rail line
years.p: The debut lands on year-end lists at NPR, Pitchfork and The A.V. Club.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the record deals with Clarke's year of substance abuse and debauchery. Wikipedia's Sunbather article says Nick Steinhardt of Touche Amore designed both covers.

q: They took us under their wing.
years.h: Russian Circles take the young band on a US run
years.p: The Chicago trio had Deafheaven on the road in November. McCoy remembers it that way.

years.cap: George Clarke on stage in Barcelona, May 2012
years.h: Three and a half months on the road, and the first lineup is gone
years.p: After the long run, drummer Trevor Deschryver quit and bassist Derek Prine left over money trouble.
years.xp:
Red Bull Music Academy has the 2012 stretch as a February European tour with Heirophant, South by Southwest, then six weeks with Russian Circles, about three and a half months straight. "It breaks you down way more than you think," Clarke told the interviewer.

Wikipedia says early members left over the difficulty of life on the road and earning little to no money.

years.h: A Mogwai cover on a split with Bosse-de-Nage
years.p: The Flenser EP has Deafheaven playing "Punk Rock" and "Cody" from Come On Die Young. A remastered demo vinyl also comes out on Sargent House that year.

years.h: [[Daniel Tracy|c1673fe1-bd6d-42dc-9a07-675106753a68]] takes the drums as Nick Bassett leaves
years.p: Tracy puts his own style on songs Clarke and McCoy had already framed.

eras.title: Pink sky over metal
eras.text: Sunbather gets a metal band argued about in places that never cover metal, and the argument books them festivals.

years.cap: Kerry McCoy on stage with Deafheaven, 2013
years.h: McCoy stacks about four guitar tracks a song on a Les Paul
years.p: The six days at Atomic Garden in January run on Jack Shirley's engineering and production, plus a lot of McCoy.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the album went to two-inch analog tape at roughly eight hours a day, and Tracy tracked most of his drums on day one. Clarke and McCoy wrote it in their apartment the year before.

years.cap: Deafheaven at Bottom of the Hill, San Francisco, July 2013
years.h: [[Shiv Mehra|94b213fd-9628-49e5-8e10-fbf57e32a589]] and bassist Stephen Clark join, and the band tours as five
years.p: Clarke and McCoy stay the songwriters while the new members take the live shows.

years.h: Sunbather comes in the pink of the sun through closed eyelids
years.p: Nick Steinhardt designed the cover from a photo by Ryan Aylsworth to match that color. Pitchfork gave the record an 8.9.
years.xp:
Metacritic scored it 92 out of 100 from 18 reviews and later called it the best-reviewed major album of 2013, per Wikipedia. It debuted at No. 130 on the Billboard 200, with 3,720 first-week copies reported, and topped year-end metal lists at Pitchfork, Rolling Stone and Stereogum.

The interlude "Please Remember" has Stephane Paut of [[Alcest|dd77b8da-cdc7-46b8-8a7f-10894ca0490e]] reading from Milan Kundera's The Unbearable Lightness of Being.

years.h: A woman sunbathing in a rich neighborhood names the album
years.p: Clarke has said he was a poor 22-year-old watching her.
years.xp: Clarke describes the theme as an unattainable wealthy, beautiful life, and on the title: "It is the sadness and frustration and anger that comes with striving for perfection." On "Windows," a recording of McCoy during a drug purchase sits beside a street preacher. McCoy has spoken publicly about struggling with prescription opioid addiction.

years.cap: Clarke and McCoy on stage, August 2013
years.h: Traditional black metal fans say shoegaze doesn't count
years.p: They dismissed the pairing. Then the record's success turned the argument into festival slots.

years.h: Australia for the first time, then back out with Between the Buried and Me
years.p: Deafheaven play Australia in January, then support Between the Buried and Me across North America in February and March.

years.h: Adult Swim puts out "From the Kettle Onto the Coil"
years.p: It comes in the network's weekly singles series. Clarke said it followed the Sunbather formula.

years.cap: Creepers, the side project of Daniel Tracy and Shiv Mehra
years.h: Two Deafheaven members put out a psychedelic rock record as Creepers
years.p: Tracy and Mehra's Lush comes out on All Black Recording Company, the label of Clarke and Derek Prine.

eras.title: Anti-, and the long songs
eras.text: Anti- becomes the new label, Jack Shirley stays in the producer's chair, and "Honeycomb" earns a Grammy nomination.

years.h: Anti- releases New Bermuda, recorded live in April
years.p: The band cut it in Oakland and Palo Alto with Jack Shirley. Pitchfork gave it 9.0, and Spin ranked it first on its 20 best metal albums of 2015.
years.xp:
Allison Schulnik painted the cover, an oil painting. Wikipedia says it peaked at No. 63 on the Billboard 200.

Clarke told Red Bull Music Academy the pressure gave him night terrors about failing.

years.h: [[Chris Johnson|ddda8caf-1694-49b5-acf8-7b282a5b4954]] replaces Stephen Clark on bass
years.p: He is still in the band. Mike Sullivan filled in on bass in 2017.

years.h: Ordinary Corrupt Human Love sets the soft against the loud
years.p: Seven tracks, recorded in February 2018 at 25th Street in Oakland. [[Chelsea Wolfe|60e8e938-365e-4429-a141-4c79eb49588d]] sings on "Night People."
years.xp: The title comes from Graham Greene's The End of the Affair, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork gave the album 8.5.

years.cap: Deafheaven at Fete Music Hall, Providence, November 2018
years.h: Grammy voters nominate "Honeycomb" for Best Metal Performance
years.p: The lead single from Ordinary Corrupt Human Love is the band's first Grammy nomination. Clarke told Billboard the band felt foreign to that world.

eras.title: Just the beauty
eras.text: A B-side, a live-in-studio farewell to a decade, then an album with no screaming.

years.h: "Black Brick" shows up as a B-side
years.p: It follows Ordinary Corrupt Human Love by about seven months.

years.h: 10 Years Gone marks a decade with a live-in-studio set
years.p: The band records its songs live. The release note thanks fans for sticking with them while they make new music for 2021.
years.xp: Deafheaven recorded Infinite Granite from August to October 2020, at Atomic Garden East in Oakland, Electric Bunker in Boston and Justin Meldal-Johnsen's home studio in Glendale, according to Wikipedia.

years.cap: Deafheaven in 2021, around the release of Infinite Granite
years.h: The band wipes its social media, then posts a date: 08.20.21
years.p: Two days later it releases "Great Mass of Color," with Clarke singing clean instead of screaming.

years.h: [[Justin Meldal-Johnsen|673f2360-45c1-43d3-b0d2-cf6d798b2fdd]] produces Infinite Granite, and Clarke sings
years.p: On Sargent House, the album leaves black metal mostly behind. The Guardian gave it 5 stars, and Metal Hammer said the band had lost some intensity.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 82 from 21 reviews. Chelsea Jade adds vocals on two tracks. The A.V. Club called it only the beauty, in what it read as a blur of pleasure.

eras.title: Back to the speed
eras.text: A festival takeover, a new label, and an album that puts the screaming back in.

years.cap: Deafheaven on the DWP Stage at Aftershock Festival, October 2023
years.h: Roadburn gets Sunbather one night and Infinite Granite the next
years.p: Deafheaven headline the Dutch festival in April, playing Sunbather in full for its tenth anniversary on one night and Infinite Granite in full on another.
years.xp: Guitarist Shaun Durkan toured with the band in 2023 and 2024, per Wikipedia.

years.h: After Sargent House, Deafheaven sign with Roadrunner Records
years.p: The band announces the move on February 7.

years.h: Lonely People with Power brings the screaming back
years.p: Twelve tracks, none over ten minutes, on Roadrunner. "Magnolia" was the first single, with a music video.
years.xp:
Three of the twelve are short "Incidental" tracks with guests Jae Matthews of Boy Harsher and Paul Banks of Interpol, per Consequence. Clarke said the band took the songwriting exercises from Infinite Granite and applied them here.

Consequence named Deafheaven its Heavy Band of the Year for the record.

years.big: "I miss the power and I miss the speed"
q: I miss the power and I miss the speed.
years.h: After the clean-vocal tours, Clarke wants to be wild again
years.p: Singing clean meant restraint onstage, Clarke told Consequence, and that didn't fit how he wanted to perform.

years.h: McCoy promises an EP that is "the heaviest thing we've ever released"
years.p: Kerry McCoy announced plans for the EP in 2026, per Wikipedia.

sources.title: Red Bull Music Academy: Deafheaven interview
Consequence: Heavy Band of the Year 2025
